note: Hand-placed reference points for comparison, from party platforms, voting records, survey reports and historians' accounts. Scale -1 to +1 on the axes in axes.json; an axis is left out where the group had no clear position (historical parties never weighed in on AI or gender identity). Approximate and meant for fun, not a measurement. Generated by scripts/revisions/rev_2026_10_13_profiles.py.

categories.name: Voter types
categories.about: The nine groups in Pew Research Center's political typology of American voters.

categories.name: Presidents
categories.about: Placed from their record in office, not their rhetoric.

categories.name: US history
categories.about: Parties and movements from earlier eras, compared only on issues they took positions on.

categories.name: Ideologies
categories.about: Schools of thought, as their mainstream US advocates would apply them.

categories.name: Abroad
categories.about: Parties in other democracies, translated onto US-style issues. Their home debates differ, so treat these loosely.

profiles.name: Progressive Democrats
profiles.about: The party's left wing: Medicare for All, Green New Deal, criminal justice reform, a smaller military budget.

profiles.name: Mainstream Democrats
profiles.about: The party's center: protect and expand the ACA, climate investment, abortion rights, alliances abroad.

profiles.name: Moderate Democrats
profiles.about: Blue Dogs and swing-district Democrats: fiscal caution, energy production, tougher on the border and crime than the party's base.

profiles.name: Abundance liberals
profiles.about: YIMBY, build-more Democrats: zoning reform, permitting reform, clean energy buildout, high-skill immigration, pro-technology.

profiles.name: Democratic Socialists
profiles.about: Democratic Socialists of America: public ownership of key industries, strong unions, sharply reduced inequality, anti-war.

profiles.name: Green Party
profiles.about: Environment first, nonviolence, grassroots democracy, social justice, ranked-choice voting.

profiles.name: Civil libertarian left
profiles.about: ACLU-style liberals: free speech for everyone, privacy, due process, church-state separation, skeptical of police and surveillance.

profiles.name: Independents and centrists
profiles.about: Mixed views, mostly near the middle, wary of both parties and of strong presidents.

profiles.name: Libertarian Party
profiles.about: Minimal government in both the economy and personal life; free trade; restraint abroad.

profiles.name: Mises Caucus libertarians
profiles.about: The Libertarian Party's current leadership: anti-state and anti-war, but culturally conservative and restrictive on immigration.

profiles.name: Never-Trump conservatives
profiles.about: Pre-Trump conservatives who broke with the party: free trade, alliances, institutional checks, moderate social conservatism.

profiles.name: Mainstream Republicans
profiles.about: Today's party: border enforcement, tariffs, tax cuts, traditional social views, skeptical of institutions.

profiles.name: America First / MAGA
profiles.about: The movement around Trump: mass deportation, high tariffs, a strong presidency, fighting the 'deep state', no new foreign wars.

profiles.name: House Freedom Caucus
profiles.about: The House's hard-right bloc: deep spending cuts, border hawks, social conservatives, willing to buck party leaders.

profiles.name: National conservatives
profiles.about: NatCon intellectuals: restrict immigration, protect industry, use government for families and workers, skeptical of foreign wars.

profiles.name: Religious conservatives
profiles.about: Faith and family first: ending abortion, religious liberty, traditional marriage, parental rights in schools.

profiles.name: Tech right
profiles.about: Silicon Valley's turn rightward: deregulate AI and crypto, build fast, high-skill immigration, against DEI and speech rules.

profiles.name: Post-liberal right
profiles.about: Catholic integralists and 'common good' conservatives: use state power for traditional morality, families and workers.

profiles.name: Progressive Left
profiles.about: Young, highly educated and very liberal on every issue; want sweeping change to the system.

profiles.name: Establishment Liberals
profiles.about: Liberal but pragmatic; trust institutions more and prefer compromise and incremental change.

profiles.name: Democratic Mainstays
profiles.about: The party's largest and most diverse bloc: liberal on economics, more moderate and religious on social issues.

profiles.name: Outsider Left
profiles.about: Young, very liberal and frustrated with the system and with the Democratic Party itself.

profiles.name: Stressed Sideliners
profiles.about: Politically disengaged, financially stressed, mixed views: liberal-leaning on economics, conservative-leaning on culture.

profiles.name: Ambivalent Right
profiles.about: Younger, right-leaning on economics and immigration but moderate on abortion, marijuana and same-sex marriage.

profiles.name: Populist Right
profiles.about: Less affluent conservatives: very restrictive on immigration, critical of big business and free trade, distrust elites.

profiles.name: Committed Conservatives
profiles.about: Traditional pro-business conservatives: low taxes, limited government, free trade, an active role in the world.

profiles.name: Faith and Flag Conservatives
profiles.about: The most conservative group: religion should shape law and public life, strongly traditional, intensely partisan.

profiles.name: Theodore Roosevelt
profiles.about: Trust-busting, food and drug safety, national parks, a big navy and a broad view of presidential power.

profiles.name: Woodrow Wilson
profiles.about: Income tax, Federal Reserve, lower tariffs, the League of Nations, and wartime limits on speech.

profiles.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
profiles.about: The New Deal: Social Security, labor rights, public works, bank regulation; four terms and a wartime presidency.

profiles.name: Harry Truman
profiles.about: Fair Deal, proposed national health insurance, desegregated the military, NATO and the Marshall Plan.

profiles.name: Dwight Eisenhower
profiles.about: Kept the New Deal, built the interstates, enforced school desegregation, balanced budgets, alliances abroad.

profiles.name: John F. Kennedy
profiles.about: Tax cuts and trade expansion, a civil rights bill, the space race, a hard line against the Soviets.

profiles.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
profiles.about: The Great Society: Medicare, Medicaid, the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts, open immigration, and the Vietnam escalation.

profiles.name: Richard Nixon
profiles.about: Created the EPA, imposed wage and price controls, law and order, opened China, and Watergate.

profiles.name: Jimmy Carter
profiles.about: Deregulated airlines and trucking, energy conservation, human rights abroad, the Camp David Accords.

profiles.name: Ronald Reagan
profiles.about: Big tax cuts, deregulation, a military buildup, the 1986 immigration amnesty, and a hard line on the Soviet Union.

profiles.name: George H. W. Bush
profiles.about: Raised taxes to cut the deficit, the Clean Air Act and the ADA, the Gulf War coalition, NAFTA talks.

profiles.name: Bill Clinton
profiles.about: Balanced budgets, welfare reform, NAFTA, the 1994 crime bill and assault weapons ban, DOMA.

profiles.name: George W. Bush
profiles.about: Tax cuts, No Child Left Behind, Medicare drug benefit, the Patriot Act, and the Iraq and Afghanistan wars.

profiles.name: Barack Obama
profiles.about: The ACA, Wall Street reform, the Paris climate deal, DACA, same-sex marriage support, drone strikes.

profiles.name: Donald Trump
profiles.about: Tariffs, tax cuts, border enforcement and deportations, deregulation, an expansive view of presidential power.

profiles.name: Joe Biden
profiles.about: Infrastructure and climate spending, kept and added tariffs on China, union support, student debt relief, aid to Ukraine.

profiles.name: Federalists
profiles.about: Hamilton and Adams: a strong national government and bank, tariffs for industry, the Alien and Sedition Acts.

profiles.name: Jeffersonian Republicans
profiles.about: Jefferson and Madison: limited federal power, farmers over bankers, church-state separation, against the Sedition Act.

profiles.name: Jacksonian Democrats
profiles.about: Andrew Jackson's party: kill the national bank, power to the common (white) man, a forceful president, westward expansion.

profiles.name: Whigs
profiles.about: Henry Clay's American System: tariffs, a national bank, roads and canals, moral reform, and checks on 'King Andrew'.

profiles.name: Radical Republicans
profiles.about: Abolition, Reconstruction, the 14th and 15th Amendments, federal protection for freed people's rights and votes.

profiles.name: Gilded Age Republicans
profiles.about: Party of business and high tariffs: gold standard, light regulation, railroads and industry first.

profiles.name: People's (Populist) Party
profiles.about: Farmers and workers against railroads and banks: public ownership of railroads, an income tax, direct elections.

profiles.name: Socialist Party (Debs era)
profiles.about: Eugene Debs's party: public ownership, labor rights, women's suffrage, opposition to World War I.

profiles.name: Bull Moose Progressives
profiles.about: Theodore Roosevelt's party: trust-busting, conservation, social insurance, direct democracy, a strong nation.

profiles.name: New Deal Democrats
profiles.about: FDR-to-LBJ coalition: Social Security, unions, public works, Cold War internationalism, socially traditional.

profiles.name: Rockefeller Republicans
profiles.about: Liberal Northeastern Republicans: pro-business but accepting the welfare state, civil rights, environmental laws, internationalism.

profiles.name: Goldwater conservatives
profiles.about: Barry Goldwater's insurgency: roll back the New Deal, states' rights, all-out anti-communism.

profiles.name: Great Society liberals
profiles.about: Johnson-era liberals: war on poverty, Medicare, civil rights and voting rights, federal aid to schools, Cold War resolve.

profiles.name: New Left
profiles.about: Student radicals and the counterculture: against the Vietnam War, for civil rights, sexual freedom and participatory democracy.

profiles.name: Reagan coalition
profiles.about: Tax cuts, deregulation, free trade, strong defense and traditional values, uniting business and religious conservatives.

profiles.name: New Democrats
profiles.about: Clinton-era centrists: balanced budgets, welfare reform, free trade, tough on crime.

profiles.name: Contract with America Republicans
profiles.about: Newt Gingrich's House majority: balanced budget amendment, welfare reform, tough-on-crime laws, term limits.

profiles.name: Bush–Romney Republicans
profiles.about: Lower taxes, free trade, an active foreign policy, compassionate conservatism and respect for institutions.

profiles.name: Tea Party
profiles.about: Grassroots revolt against bailouts, the ACA and federal spending: cut government, follow the Constitution, primary the moderates.

profiles.name: Occupy Wall Street
profiles.about: 'We are the 99%': against bailouts, inequality and corporate power in politics.

profiles.name: Anarcho-capitalism
profiles.about: Abolish the state; private property, markets and voluntary contracts provide everything, including courts and security.

profiles.name: Classical liberalism
profiles.about: Limited constitutional government, free markets and free trade, individual rights, free speech and the rule of law.

profiles.name: Neoliberalism
profiles.about: Markets with a safety net: free trade, open immigration, carbon pricing, build more housing, trust expertise.

profiles.name: Social democracy
profiles.about: Regulated capitalism with a universal welfare state: public health care, strong unions, high taxes, broad equality.

profiles.name: Eco-socialism
profiles.about: Capitalism is driving climate collapse: public ownership, degrowth or planned transition, global climate justice.

profiles.name: Marxism–Leninism
profiles.about: State ownership of the economy under a single vanguard party, in the Soviet and Chinese tradition.

profiles.name: Left anarchism
profiles.about: No state, no bosses: mutual aid, worker and community self-management, abolish police, prisons and borders.

profiles.name: Christian democracy
profiles.about: Catholic social teaching in politics: a social market economy, family policy, moral tradition and international cooperation.

profiles.name: Neoconservatism
profiles.about: Spread democracy with American power: strong military, interventions abroad, free markets, moderate social conservatism.

profiles.name: Paleoconservatism
profiles.about: Old Right: tradition, local community and national identity; against mass immigration, free trade and foreign wars.

profiles.name: UK Labour
profiles.about: Britain's center-left governing party: the NHS, workers' rights, clean energy, housebuilding, NATO.

profiles.name: UK Conservatives
profiles.about: Britain's center-right: lower taxes, Brexit, lower immigration, but firm support for the NHS and strict gun laws.

profiles.name: Reform UK
profiles.about: Nigel Farage's insurgent right: net-zero immigration, scrap net-zero climate targets, anti-establishment.

profiles.name: Canadian Liberals
profiles.about: Canada's governing center-left: public health care, carbon pricing (now scaled back), high immigration, strict gun laws.

profiles.name: Canadian Conservatives
profiles.about: Canada's center-right: cut taxes and the carbon tax, build homes and pipelines, tougher on crime; keeps public health care.

profiles.name: Nordic Social Democrats
profiles.about: Sweden's and Denmark's center-left: universal welfare, high taxes, flexible labor markets, free trade, and (in Denmark) strict immigration.

profiles.name: German Christian Democrats
profiles.about: Germany's center-right: social market economy, fiscal discipline, tighter asylum rules, strong support for the EU and NATO.

profiles.name: German Greens
profiles.about: Climate-first progressives who became a governing party: rapid energy transition, civil liberties, pro-EU, firm on Ukraine.

profiles.name: French National Rally
profiles.about: Marine Le Pen's party: sharply cut immigration, protect French industry, keep a generous welfare state, skeptical of the EU.

profiles.name: Macron's Renaissance
profiles.about: France's liberal center: pro-business reforms, a raised retirement age, strict secularism, a stronger EU.
